meta.description: Housing market dashboard data â€” NYC suburban markets for home purchase research

mortgage_rates.rate_driver: Iran conflict + May CPI 3.8% â€” rates ticking up week-over-week
mortgage_rates.notes: 30yr at 6.51% (up from 6.50% prior week). 15yr at 5.85% (up from 5.79%). 20yr at 6.54%. Above conforming limit ($832,750) adds ~0.10-0.15% for jumbo.

primary_markets.name: Floral Park

downtown.character: Quaint mid-century main street with three commercial corridors â€” Covert Ave, Tulip Ave, and Jericho Turnpike. Flat, sidewalked, and friendly for daily errands with a classic Long Island village feel.
downtown.verdict: Genuinely walkable for a Long Island village â€” daily errands and the LIRR on foot, but nightlife variety is thin.

primary_markets.notes: Strong LIRR access; Nassau County taxes fully combined including school district.

primary_markets.name: Rockville Centre

downtown.character: The most authentically walkable downtown of the LI primary markets. North Park Avenue is a tree-lined strip dense with restaurants, bars, and boutiques â€” over 98 dining and drinking establishments in the village, with genuine evening foot traffic rare for Long Island.
highlights: North Park Avenue dining & bar strip
downtown.verdict: Best LI primary market downtown â€” rare suburb where you can leave the car home for evenings out.

primary_markets.notes: Higher tax burden than Floral Park; well-regarded school district.

primary_markets.name: Maplewood

downtown.character: One of the best downtowns in the entire NYC suburban ring. Maplewood Avenue is a dense, diverse strip with fine dining, pubs, a jazz scene, and a farmer's market â€” all in a 5-minute pedestrian loop connecting the train station to Memorial Park.
highlights: Maplewood Avenue village strip (train to park)
Memorial Park adjacent to village center
downtown.verdict: Car-optional for evenings, weekends, and errands â€” a true 'village in the suburbs' with constant foot traffic.

primary_markets.notes: Added for NJ geographic diversity and NYC spillover demand angle. Note higher NJ tax burden.

primary_markets.name: Pelham

downtown.character: Pre-automobile street grid with continuous sidewalks and the Metro-North station at the center of it all. Fifth Avenue and Wolfs Lane flank the station with independent shops, a Michelin-recognized steakhouse, and the Pelham Art Center â€” more cultural depth than comparably-sized LI villages.
highlights: Fifth Ave / Wolfs Lane (two-sided main street)
downtown.verdict: Genuinely walkable and well-programmed â€” station-centered grid is a structural advantage over car-first LI suburbs.

primary_markets.notes: Fastest commute of all markets. Metro-North to GCT is the key differentiator vs. LIRR to Penn.

research_markets.name: Rockaway Park

downtown.character: Beach community with surf-casual vibe. Rockaway Beach Blvd is the main strip with bars, cafes, and surf shops; the Atlantic Ocean boardwalk is the social center.
downtown.verdict: Seasonally walkable and charming in summer, thins out off-season. Beach-town strip rather than traditional village downtown.

research_markets.notes: Lowest taxes of all markets due to NYC Class 1 assessment structure. Flood zone risk (FEMA Zone AE) adds ~$2-4K/yr flood insurance. Schools vary widely â€” Scholars' Academy 9/10 but admission not guaranteed by address.

research_markets.name: Larchmont

downtown.character: Quintessential Sound Shore village with two downtown nodes â€” boutique shops, farm-to-table dining, and antique stores all steps from the Metro-North platform.
highlights: Manor Park waterfront on Long Island Sound
downtown.verdict: One of Westchester's most walkable downtowns. Can skip the car for daily errands â€” true village feel at its best.

research_markets.notes: Above $700K-$1M budget ceiling. Shares Mamaroneck UFSD (A+, #24 NY) with Town of Mamaroneck at a ~$550K premium. Fast-moving market.

research_markets.name: Bronxville

downtown.character: Deliberately designed Gilded Age village where train station, village hall, library, and dining are all within a 0.4-mile radius. Iconic Tudor-style architecture along Pondfield Road.
downtown.verdict: Highest walk score of all 10 markets. Designed for pedestrians from inception â€” most cohesive walkable village in NYC suburbs. No supermarket within village limits.

research_markets.notes: Best schools of all 10 markets (10/10 GS, 91% math proficiency). Tiny village â€” 0.6 sq mi, ~6,200 residents. Above budget for SFH. Moderate tax vs. Westchester peers.

research_markets.name: Sea Cliff
research_markets.niche_rank: #75 Best Elementary in NY (Sea Cliff Elem)

downtown.character: Quirky artsy Victorian hillside village with jewel-toned gingerbread houses on winding bluff-top streets above Long Island Sound. Bohemian energy with indie boutiques and a live-music gastropub.
downtown.verdict: Genuinely charming and walkable within its 1 sq mile footprint â€” unusual for Long Island. LIRR Oyster Bay branch requires Jamaica transfer (65-75 min total) â€” commute is the primary headwind.

research_markets.notes: Previously removed from primary dashboard. LIRR Oyster Bay branch requires Jamaica transfer â€” longest commute of all markets. DOM rising sharply (32 to 72 days) â€” negotiating leverage possible. Strong schools.

research_markets.name: Mamaroneck

downtown.character: Lively harborside village with cafe-lined Mamaroneck Avenue connecting Metro-North station to Long Island Sound. Multicultural main street with authentic diversity and a working harbor marina.
highlights: Harbor Island Park (44 acres on the Sound)
Active waterfront marina with Sound views
downtown.verdict: Genuinely walkable and well-rounded. More vibrant and diverse than Larchmont. Best value play: same A+ schools at ~$550K lower price. Tax trajectory rising sharply is the key risk.

research_markets.notes: Best value play in Westchester â€” same A+ SD as Larchmont (~$550K lower median). Some inventory $750K-$950K. Tax levy rising: +9.95% in 2025, double-digit increases projected 2026-2027.

research_markets.name: Montclair

downtown.character: Bloomfield Avenue forms a mile-plus spine through four distinct commercial districts â€” independent bookstores, art galleries, farm-to-table dining, the Wellmont Theater, Montclair Art Museum, and one of NJ's most celebrated coffee scenes. One of the most ethnically diverse suburbs in the entire NYC metro.
highlights: Four walkable commercial districts (Center, Upper, Walnut, Watchung)
downtown.verdict: Richer arts and dining scene than any other market in this set. Car-optional for evenings and weekends â€” six NJ Transit stations mean most residents walk to the train.

research_markets.notes: Similar lifestyle to Maplewood but larger and more urban. Avg tax bill $22,487 (effective ~2.31% on market value; NJ statutory rate ~3.38% on assessed). School district rated Niche A with diverse academic profile.

research_markets.name: Westfield
research_markets.transit_note: Raritan Valley Line to Newark Penn, then NJT or PATH â€” no Midtown Direct

downtown.character: Broad Street forms a genuine Main Street with continuous storefronts, sidewalk dining, independent boutiques, and a historic train depot adjacent to the NJ Transit platform. One of the best-preserved traditional downtowns in the NYC metro area.
highlights: Broad Street dining and retail corridor (200+ establishments)
Mindowaskin Park (100-acre green anchor adjacent to downtown)
Westfield train station at the edge of the commercial core
downtown.verdict: One of New Jersey's best Main Streets â€” station-adjacent, independently-owned mix, and genuine evening foot traffic. The Raritan Valley Line's Newark transfer is the primary commute trade-off vs. Midtown Direct towns like Chatham.

research_markets.notes: Top-ranked Union County district (Niche A+, GS 9/10 â€” consistently top 5-10% in NJ). Raritan Valley Line requires a Newark Penn transfer adding ~15 min vs. Midtown Direct lines. Price point broadly similar to Maplewood with comparable or better schools. Lower taxes than Essex County (Maplewood, Montclair).

research_markets.name: Chatham

downtown.character: Station-centered Main Street where the NJ Transit Midtown Direct stops steps from T.M. Ward Coffee Co., Crew cafÃ©, Scalini Fideli, and a tree-lined stretch of local shops. Old-fashioned small-town feel with wide sidewalks and dog-friendly patios â€” only 2.4 sq mi total.
highlights: Main Street / NJ Transit station (walkable loop)
downtown.verdict: Charming and intimate rather than expansive â€” more like a true small town than a suburban village strip. Midtown Direct is the key asset: no Secaucus transfer, straight to Penn Station.

research_markets.notes: Morris County taxes are lower than Essex; Chatham SD ranked top-10% in NJ (Niche A+, 97% college placement). Borough vs Township distinction â€” Borough has the walkable downtown and train station.

research_markets.name: Wykagyl (New Rochelle)
research_markets.transit_note: New Haven Line ~30-40 min station-to-GCT, BUT New Rochelle station is ~3 mi south â€” drive/Bee-Line bus to train adds 10-15 min; not a walk-to-rail neighborhood
research_markets.niche_rank: North-end NR schools: Ward Elem B+, Albert Leonard Middle A-, NR High A-

downtown.character: Affluent, almost entirely residential north-end neighborhood of New Rochelle (zip 10804) â€” sprawling early-to-mid-20th-century homes (Tudor, Mediterranean villa, classic colonial) on large landscaped lots beside the Wykagyl Country Club. The only commercial node is the Wykagyl Shopping Center strip on North Avenue; daily life is car-dependent.
highlights: Wykagyl Country Club & green, leafy residential parks
Historic Thomas Paine Cottage Museum nearby
downtown.verdict: A wealthy, quiet, car-first suburb â€” the opposite of a walkable village. You drive for everything, including to the train ~3 miles away. Big period homes and strong north-end schools, but well above budget and the weakest walkability/commute of the Westchester set.

research_markets.notes: ABOVE BUDGET â€” Wykagyl Park median sale ~$1.7M (avg ~$1.74M, +22% YoY); broader-area median ~$1.4M including some North Ave co-ops. Wealthier than ~99% of US neighborhoods; dominated by large 4-5BR homes. Served by New Rochelle City SD but north-end schools rate higher than the city overall (Ward Elem B+, Albert Leonard Middle A-, NR High A-). Key trade-off: ~3 mi from the Metro-North station, so unlike Pelham/Larchmont it is NOT a walk-to-rail town. 10804 carries among the highest tax bills in New Rochelle (~$21K).

research_markets.name: Port Washington
research_markets.transit_note: Port Washington Branch â€” direct service, no Jamaica transfer required; ~47-57 min to Penn Station

downtown.character: Waterfront village on a peninsula jutting into Manhasset Bay. Main Street runs from the LIRR terminus down to the harbor with restaurants, boutiques, and a working marina. The waterfront esplanade and Manorhaven Beach Park anchor weekend life. One of Long Island's most scenic and coveted commuter towns.
highlights: Main Street dining and boutique corridor
downtown.verdict: The most desirable LIRR Gold Coast commuter town â€” waterfront lifestyle, direct no-transfer service to Penn, and top schools. Premium pricing (~$1.15M median) reflects it.

research_markets.notes: Port Washington Branch is one of only two LIRR branches with direct Penn Station service (no Jamaica transfer) â€” a meaningful commute quality advantage over branches requiring a transfer. Above the $832,750 conforming loan limit; jumbo required for most purchases. Nassau County taxes are lower than RVC despite strong schools. Previously in primary dashboard; re-added as research market.

research_markets.name: New Rochelle
research_markets.transit_note: New Haven Line â€” express ~30 min to GCT, locals ~40 min; downtown homes walkable to station
research_markets.niche_rank: #166 Best SD in NY (New Rochelle City SD)

downtown.character: A genuine small-city downtown in the middle of a transit-oriented building boom. The core around Library Green, North Avenue, and Huguenot Street is filling with new mixed-use towers, ground-floor retail, and restaurants â€” all within a short walk of the Metro-North/Amtrak station. More urban and less 'village' than its Sound Shore neighbors.
highlights: North Avenue / Library Green downtown core
New Rochelle Metro-North + Amtrak station (walkable TOD district)
Rapidly expanding restaurant and high-rise residential scene
downtown.verdict: The most urban, fastest-changing downtown of the Westchester set â€” strong walkability and a quick New Haven Line commute, though the large, diverse school district rates lower than premium peers like Bronxville or Larchmont.

research_markets.notes: PRICE INCLUDES ALL HOMES (condos + SFH) â€” Zillow does not publish a city-level single-family-only series for New Rochelle, so the auto-refresh uses the combined all-homes ZHVI (~$900K). True SFH-only price is likely $1.0M-$1.1M based on Redfin/PropertyShark SFH listings; the all-homes figure is dragged down by New Rochelle's large co-op and condo stock. City structure means combined city + school + county tax. Fastest Westchester commute in the research set (~30 min express to GCT). New Rochelle City SD is large and diverse â€” Niche A- (#166 NY), GreatSchools mid-range (~5/10), below premium Westchester peers. Seed value $1.05M will be corrected to the live SFR figure on next Wednesday refresh.

research_markets.name: South Orange
research_markets.transit_note: Morris & Essex Line (Midtown Direct) — direct service to Penn Station, no transfer; ~50-58 min

downtown.character: Compact village center with South Orange Ave as its spine — independent restaurants, cafes, a bookstore, and the Baird Community Center all walkable from the NJ Transit platform. Seton Hall University adds energy and a year-round dining scene.
downtown.verdict: Tight, walkable village center with genuine neighborhood character. Shares schools and some amenities with Maplewood — often considered the same lifestyle market at a slight price discount.

research_markets.notes: Shares the South Orange-Maplewood School District (SOMSD) with Maplewood — same schools as the primary market at a typically lower price point. Strong Midtown Direct access. NJ high taxes apply (~2.8% effective rate). Good value play vs Maplewood for buyers flexible on town identity.

research_markets.name: West Orange
research_markets.transit_note: Morris & Essex Line (Midtown Direct) — Brick Church or Highland Ave stations; ~45-55 min to Penn

downtown.character: Larger, more suburban town than its Orange neighbors — spread across multiple distinct neighborhoods. Main Street in the Pleasantdale area has some retail, but West Orange is largely car-dependent. The Turtle Back Zoo, South Mountain Reservation, and Eagle Rock Reservation are major draws.
downtown.verdict: More suburban and car-dependent than South Orange or Maplewood. Trades walkability for space, lower prices, and excellent outdoor recreation access.

research_markets.notes: Most affordable of the Essex County NJ markets in this set. West Orange Public Schools are decent (Niche B+, GreatSchools 6/10) but below the South Orange-Maplewood and Montclair districts. Multiple NJ Transit stations (Brick Church, Highland Ave) with Midtown Direct access. Larger lot sizes and more suburban feel than Maplewood or South Orange.

research_markets.name: Rutherford
research_markets.transit_note: Main Line / Bergen County Line — Midtown Direct to Penn Station; ~30-38 min, one of the fastest NJ Transit commutes in the NYC metro

downtown.character: Park Avenue forms a genuine Main Street with independent restaurants, a bookstore, coffee shops, and a historic movie theater — all within a 5-minute walk of the NJ Transit station. One of Bergen County's most walkable and charming commuter downtowns.
downtown.verdict: Punches well above its price point — walkable village center, fast Midtown Direct commute, and solid schools at Bergen County prices. One of the better value propositions in the NJ market set.

research_markets.notes: Bergen County NJ — among the fastest NJ Transit commutes to Penn (30-38 min Midtown Direct, no transfer). Rutherford Borough SD rates Niche A-, GreatSchools 7/10 — solid but not elite. Lower prices than Essex County peers (Maplewood, Montclair). Walkable downtown is a standout for Bergen County. Flood risk in some areas near Passaic River — check FEMA zone before committing.

research_markets.name: Essex Fells
research_markets.transit_note: No station in town — drive to Mountain Ave or Caldwell (Morris & Essex Line); ~50-65 min total door-to-door to Penn

downtown.character: Essex Fells has no commercial center — it is an exclusively residential borough of ~2,100 people. Daily errands require driving to neighboring Caldwell or West Caldwell. The appeal is entirely the housing stock: large Tudors and colonials on wooded lots in a quiet, private community.
highlights: Wooded residential lots — quiet, private borough
downtown.verdict: No walkability to speak of — fully car-dependent. The draw is the neighborhood itself: exclusive, wooded, extremely safe, with top-tier schools and low taxes by NJ standards. A lifestyle buy, not a transit-oriented buy.

research_markets.notes: One of NJ's most exclusive small boroughs — ~2,100 residents, no commercial zone, minimum lot sizes, and among the top school districts in Essex County (Niche A+, GreatSchools 9/10). Unusually low effective tax rate for NJ (~1.75%) due to low density and favorable assessment structure. No walk-to-train — must drive to Mountain Ave or Caldwell station for Morris & Essex service. Median price near $1M puts most inventory at or above budget ceiling. Very low inventory / slow turnover.

research_markets.name: Nutley
research_markets.transit_note: No station in town — drive or bus to Clifton (Boonton Line) or Bloomfield (M&E Line); NJ Transit 192 bus direct to Port Authority; ~50-65 min door-to-door

downtown.character: Franklin Avenue is a compact Main Street with diners, Italian restaurants, a pharmacy, and local shops — a classic NJ township center. Quiet, residential, and family-oriented with a tight community feel.
downtown.verdict: Solid working-class suburb with genuine neighborhood feel. More affordable than its Essex County neighbors. No walk-to-train is the main drawback for NYC commuters.

research_markets.notes: Essex County township with no NJ Transit rail station — commute requires driving to Clifton (Boonton Line) or Bloomfield (M&E) or taking the 192 bus to Port Authority (~55-65 min). Most affordable Essex County market in this set at ~$565K median. Nutley Public Schools rate Niche A-, GreatSchools 7/10 — competitive with South Orange at a lower price point. Strong Italian-American community identity. Close to Belleville and Bloomfield.

research_markets.name: Glen Ridge
research_markets.transit_note: Montclair-Boonton Line (Midtown Direct) — Glen Ridge station; ~45-55 min to Penn Station

downtown.character: Tiny, immaculate borough centered on Ridgewood Avenue — a handful of local shops and restaurants in a quiet, tree-lined setting. Glen Ridge is primarily residential; Bloomfield and Montclair serve as its commercial hubs. Exceptionally safe and tightly-knit community.
highlights: Walk to Glen Ridge NJ Transit station
downtown.verdict: More village than downtown — the appeal is the residential streets, not the commercial scene. Borders Montclair for restaurants and shopping.

research_markets.notes: One of the highest-rated school districts in all of NJ — Glen Ridge Public Schools consistently rank Niche A+, GreatSchools 9/10. Very small borough (~7,500 residents), extremely low inventory and fast-moving market. Borders Montclair (shares some amenities). Walk-to-train via Montclair-Boonton Line (Midtown Direct). NJ high taxes but below Montclair. Premium for schools and exclusivity is real — expect competition.

research_markets.name: Verona
research_markets.transit_note: No station in town — drive or bus to Montclair Bay St or Mountain Ave (Montclair-Boonton Line); ~55-70 min door-to-door

downtown.character: Bloomfield Avenue runs through town with a modest strip of local restaurants, a hardware store, and small shops. Relaxed, residential pace — more small-town than village. Verona Park is the social anchor with a lake, tennis courts, and summer concerts.
downtown.verdict: Quiet, family-oriented suburb with good schools at a relative value. Trade-off is no direct train — car commute required to reach NJ Transit.

research_markets.notes: Verona Township — no rail station, must drive to Montclair (Bay St or Watchung Ave) or Mountain Ave for NJ Transit Midtown Direct access. Schools rate Niche A, GreatSchools 8/10 (Verona Public Schools) — strong for the price point. More affordable than Glen Ridge and Montclair neighbors. Car-dependent commute is the primary drawback.

research_markets.name: Caldwell
research_markets.transit_note: Montclair-Boonton Line (Midtown Direct) — Mountain Ave station; ~55-65 min to Penn Station

downtown.character: Bloomfield Avenue through the Caldwell business district has a genuine small-town Main Street feel — coffee shops, a deli, a bookstore, independent restaurants, and the historic Caldwell Theater. One of the more charming downtowns in Essex County given its modest size.
downtown.verdict: Underrated downtown with genuine character. More affordable than its neighbors with solid schools — a sleeper pick in Essex County.

research_markets.notes: Borough of Caldwell — most affordable of the Caldwell/Essex Fells/Verona cluster. Mountain Ave station (Montclair-Boonton Line, Midtown Direct) is accessible via short drive or walk depending on neighborhood. Caldwell-West Caldwell SD rates Niche A-, GreatSchools 7/10. Adjacent to Essex Fells (Niche A+) but in a different district. Good value anchor for the western Essex County market set.

research_markets.name: Merrick
research_markets.transit_note: Babylon Branch — most trains stop at Jamaica; select peak expresses run direct to Penn; ~45-55 min total

downtown.character: Merrick Road is the main commercial corridor with local restaurants, shops, and services — a classic South Shore Nassau County strip. Merrick station area has a small cluster of commuter-oriented dining. Primarily residential with a quiet, family-focused character.
highlights: Merrick Lake Park & Anchor Marine Park
downtown.verdict: Comfortable South Shore suburb with good schools and solid LIRR access. More car-dependent than North Shore peers but priced well below them.

research_markets.notes: South Shore Nassau County on the LIRR Babylon Branch. Strong schools (Merrick UFSD + Sanford H. Calhoun HS, Niche A, GreatSchools 8/10). Lower taxes than North Shore and Rockville Centre at a similar or lower price point. Most LIRR Babylon Branch trains stop at Jamaica — check peak express schedules for direct Penn service. Good value among Nassau County markets with top-tier schools.
